text:
jane (support): Hey team — Acme's production traffic shows a sudden p99 jump after we flipped them to falconx-extended-v2 this morning. p95 looks okay (~220ms) but p99 went from 480ms to 1.7s and we're seeing occasional 504s. They reported timeouts in their customer-facing chat.

alex (eng-oncall): Oof. Any correlation with request length or specific endpoints?

jane (support): Mostly long-context use (clients sending ~6k-8k tokens). Short requests (<=2k) are fine. Error sample: 504 from /v1/generate with body size ~7800 tokens.

mira (SRE): Dumping traces now. Can you drop a couple of request IDs?

jane (support): One example: req_id=acme-req-20240320-7a9c. Another: acme-req-20240320-9b2f.

sam (eng-runtime): I see both routed to falconx-extended-v2-shard-3 in us-west1. TLDR: tokenization differences + kvcache blowup suspicion.

lee (ml-onboard): We shipped a tokenizer merge for falconx-extended-v2 that changed how rare BPE merges are handled to improve fidelity for extended sequences. We tested perf up to 10k tokens in bench harness but maybe real-world tokenization distribution differs.

mira (SRE): Trace for acme-req-20240320-7a9c attached: <link to trace> — note big spikes in kernel p99 at step "kv_cache_restore" and long GC pauses in the runtime container around the same time.

sam (eng-runtime): Reproduced locally with a recorded payload. When token count > 5k the tokenizer emits slightly longer sequences (off by ~2-3% tokens), and our KV cache indexing code does a per-token bookkeeping pass that is O(n) with a high constant. Combined that's blowing up tail latency.

alex (eng-oncall): Any quick mitigation we can push to reduce customer impact while we fix the root cause?

lee (ml-onboard): Short-term: we can route Acme back to falconx-extended-v2-legacy-tokenizer (we still keep that variant for compatibility) — cost: slightly lower quality on edge cases but should restore previous token counts.

mira (SRE): I'll add a route rule to force legacy-tokenizer for Acme and their workspace ID until we have a fix. Sam — can you sketch a hotspot fix plan?

sam (eng-runtime): Plan: (1) mitigate in runtime by batching KV cache rebuilds instead of per-token ops (cheap config toggle to enable grouped updates), (2) patch tokenizer-to-kv index translation to avoid redundant copies, (3) long-term refactor KV cache sharding. I can backport (1) as a config flag in runtime v2.3.1.

jane (support): Do we need a canary or is it safe to flip for Acme only?

sam (eng-runtime): Flip for Acme only first. We'll enable grouped-kv-updates toggle on the pool serving falconx-extended-v2-shard-3. Expect p99 to drop back under 600ms for their long requests.

deploy-bot: deploy started: runtime-config-update grouped-kv-updates=true targeting pool falconx-extended-v2-us-west1-shard-3 (deploy id: d-20240320-831).

mira (SRE): Monitoring alerts temporary: added p99 alert threshold for falconx-extended-v2 routes at 1s until rollback completes.

deploy-bot: deploy succeeded: d-20240320-831 — rollout to 1/1 nodes in target pool complete.

sam (eng-runtime): Quick numbers from post-deploy smoke: synthetic 8k-token request p99 went from 1.7s -> 540ms on shard-3. Real traffic for Acme shows p99 trending down already.

lee (ml-onboard): We'll also run a tokenizer regression test suite with real customer payload samples. I want to add a check for produced token counts vs baseline to the onboarding CI.

alex (eng-oncall): Good. Can we also add a routing fallback so if a request times out on falconx-extended-v2, route to falconx-extended-v2-quantized or the legacy tokenizer variant automatically?

sam (eng-runtime): Yes — fallback policy exists but was not enabled for this model by default. I'll enable model-variant fallback for long-tail customers. It will add ~50ms overhead sometimes but prevent 504s.

mira (SRE): I'm handing this to postmortem queue. For ops now: (A) route Acme -> legacy tokenizer variant (done), (B) grouped-kv-updates enabled (done), (C) enable model-variant fallback (in progress).

jane (support): Acme confirms chat responsiveness is back. They saw 504s stop ~2m after your deploy. :tada:

lee (ml-onboard): Follow-ups: add token-count regression gate + add long-context stress tests with realistic message shape (not just synthetic repeated tokens). I'll open a PR for onboarding CI.

sam (eng-runtime): Follow-ups for runtime: (1) permanent commit for grouped updates + tests, (2) tighten KV cache memory accounting, (3) add metrics for tokenizer->kv index size and time per token.

alex (eng-oncall): Tickets: please link them here. We should also notify the model catalog team to update the model perf profile (document that long-context p99 previously observed).

lee (ml-onboard): Created tickets: ML-8321 (tokenizer regression tests + onboarding gate), RUNTIME-4198 (grouped-kv-updates permanent implementation), RUNTIME-4201 (enable fallback by default for new model variants).

mira (SRE): Postmortem stub created: INCIDENT-20240320-FALCONX-LONGCTX (I'll fill timeline + mitigation notes).

jane (support): I'll send a short note to Acme summarizing the root cause (tokenizer behavior increased token counts -> KV bookkeeping overhead -> tail latency) and our mitigations (routing to legacy-tokenizer + runtime toggle + permanent fixes in progress).

alex (eng-oncall): Thanks all. If anyone sees related customers affected, escalate into this thread.

mira (SRE): Closing ops loop for now; will reopen if p99 rebounds after fallback disable.

jane (support): Closing from support; Acme will reconfirm after tomorrow's morning run. Thanks :heart:
